html:
Ezana was a king of Aksum in the mid 300s CE, in what is now northern Ethiopia and Eritrea, and the first of its rulers to become Christian. He ruled from the capital, Axum; his exact dates are unknown.

By tradition his tutor was Frumentius, a Christian from Tyre who grew up at the court and was later made first bishop of Aksum by the patriarch of Alexandria.

Ezana's stone inscriptions, in Ge'ez, Greek and Sabaean, show the change. Early ones thank the war god Mahrem; later ones thank the Lord of Heaven and, in Greek, the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. His coins swapped the crescent and disc of the old gods for the cross. The Ge'ez script began to mark vowels in about his time. One inscription records a campaign against the Noba on the Nile, in the old lands of Kush. The conversion of Aksum spread slowly from the court. The Ethiopian church honours him as Saint Abreha.
